libraries.name: Risk Management
libraries.description: Real-time counterparty exposure monitoring, credit limit enforcement, margin calls, and concentration caps across settlement windows

libraries.name: Reconciliation
libraries.description: Continuous matching of internal ledger entries against counterparty acknowledgments with tolerance-based break classification and auto-resolution

libraries.name: Regulatory Compliance
libraries.description: Enforcement of reporting obligations, threshold monitoring, suspicious transaction flagging, and audit retention requirements

libraries.name: Event Infrastructure
libraries.description: Pub/sub messaging backbone providing event publishing, ordering guarantees, retry policies, and correlation tracing across the system

libraries.name: Audit and Notification
libraries.description: Immutable audit trail maintenance and operational notification routing to compliance, risk, and operations teams

libraries.name: Operations and Deployment
libraries.description: Infrastructure configuration, monitoring logic, health checks, and operational parameter management for production settlement engine

libraries.name: System Architecture
libraries.description: Cross-system invariants, component integration patterns, and high-level architecture documentation describing how all libraries interact

rationale: Seven existing libraries (LIB-01 through LIB-07) cover the functional capabilities of the settlement engine. The unroutable files ('cross_system_invariants' and 'overview') describe system-wide integration patterns, architectural invariants, and cross-library flow diagrams that do not belong to any single library. These require a new library (LIB-08 System Architecture) that captures cross-cutting architectural concerns, system-wide invariants, and orchestration patterns that govern how the seven functional libraries interact.
overlap_notes: The new System Architecture library (LIB-08) intentionally references all seven existing libraries because it documents their integration points and cross-system invariants. This is not duplication—it serves a distinct purpose of defining the contracts and invariants that bind the libraries together. Files like 'deployment_and_operations' fit cleanly into LIB-07, while 'event_pipeline', 'notification_and_audit', 'reconciliation_service', 'regulatory_compliance', 'risk_engine', 'settlement_processing', and 'transaction_validation' map to their corresponding existing libraries (LIB-05, LIB-06, LIB-03, LIB-04, LIB-02, LIB-01, LIB-01 respectively).
